Source: IBGE PIB dos Municípios, SIDRA Tabela 5938, variable 37 (PIB a
preços correntes, mil reais), SIDRA agregados API v3, queried 2026-10-09
(`_data/raw/ibge/sidra/sidra_5938_pib_*.json`); IBGE censuses 1970-2010
and 2022, resident population (`_data/raw/ibge/Ibge_pop_1970-80-91-00-10.xlsx`,
`Ibge_pop_2022 (Censo - Sidra).xlsx`); IBGE annual population estimates,
SIDRA Tabela 6579 (`sidra_6579_pop_estimate_*.json`, inspected here, not read
by the pipeline); IPCA deflator (`_data/aux/deflator_ipca_2024.csv`).
Pipeline script: `_scripts/03-controls-gdp.R`.
Interim output: `_data/interim/ibge_pib_gdp_2002_2022.rds`.
Equivalence with the recovered panel is not checked here (the notebook never
reads `_data/reference/`); the `compare_outputs` report lives in the phase 1
script 03 commit message and in the decision entries it cites.

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(readxl)
})
options(width = 110)
```

```{r read}
source("_scripts/utils/read_sidra.R")
source("_scripts/utils/interpolate_census.R")
sidra_dir <- "_data/raw/ibge/sidra"
sidra <- function(pattern) {
  map_dfr(list.files(sidra_dir, pattern = pattern, full.names = TRUE), read_sidra_json)
}
pib_raw <- sidra("^sidra_5938_pib_")
est_raw <- sidra("^sidra_6579_pop_estimate_")
pop_0010_raw <- read_excel("_data/raw/ibge/Ibge_pop_1970-80-91-00-10.xlsx", sheet = "Tabela",
                           col_types = "text")
pop_2022_raw <- read_excel("_data/raw/ibge/Ibge_pop_2022 (Censo - Sidra).xlsx", sheet = "Tabela",
                           col_types = "text", col_names = FALSE, .name_repair = "minimal")
gdp <- read_rds("_data/interim/ibge_pib_gdp_2002_2022.rds")
sample_geo <- read_rds("_data/interim/mapbiomas_deforestation_amz_1987_2023.rds") %>%
  distinct(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation)
is_geocode <- function(x) !is.na(x) & str_detect(x, "^[0-9]{7}$")
```

## Q1. What do the GDP extracts contain?

What is checked: files, series count, year span, unit, symbols, and the
sample cells without a value.

```{r q1-shape}
list.files(sidra_dir, pattern = "^sidra_5938_pib_")
pib_raw %>%
  summarise(series = n_distinct(geocode), years = paste(range(year), collapse = "-"),
            cells = n(), dots = sum(value == "..."), negative = sum(str_detect(value, "^-")),
            other = sum(!str_detect(value, "^-?[0-9]+$") & value != "..."))
pib_raw %>% filter(str_detect(value, "^-"))
pib_raw %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode, value == "...") %>%
  left_join(sample_geo, by = "geocode") %>%
  group_by(geocode, municipality.y, state_abbreviation) %>%
  summarise(years = paste(range(year), collapse = "-"), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

**Finding.** Eight files cover 2002-2023 for the 5,570 municipalities, in
integer thousands of reais (the lost CSV export carried decimals,
D-2026-10-10-b). The only symbol is "..."; one cell is negative (Guamaré,
RN, 2012, as published by IBGE, outside the sample). In the sample the
missing cells are Ipiranga do Norte and Itanhangá (MT) for 2002-2004, the
years before their installation, and Mojuí dos Campos (PA) for 2002-2012,
which the pipeline fills by the Santarém split (Q3).
**Decision.** D-2026-10-10-b; D-2026-10-10-g.
**Assertion.** `03-controls-gdp.R`, raw-state block (no classification,
5,570 series, symbols, one negative value).

## Q2. What do the population workbooks contain?

```{r q2-layout}
names(pop_0010_raw)
nrow(pop_0010_raw)
pop_0010_raw %>% summarise(across(c(`2000`, `2010`), ~ sum(.x == "...")))
pop_0010_raw %>% filter(`2010` == "...")
as.data.frame(pop_2022_raw[1:6, ])
geo_2022 <- pop_2022_raw[[2]][is_geocode(pop_2022_raw[[2]])]
length(geo_2022)
setdiff(geo_2022, pop_0010_raw$munic_id)
```

```{r q2-sample-2000}
pop_0010_raw %>%
  filter(munic_id %in% sample_geo$geocode, `2000` == "...") %>%
  select(munic_id, munic, `2000`, `2010`)
```

**Finding.** The 1970-2010 workbook has one row per municipality of the
2010 grid plus Cococi (CE), an extinct municipality with no value; "..."
marks the censuses before a municipality existed, 59 cells in 2000. The
2022 workbook (Tabela 4709) has four header rows, a Brasil row, 5,570
municipal rows and a source footer; five municipalities installed in 2013
appear only there, Mojuí dos Campos among them. In the sample the nine
Mato Grosso municipalities of task 1.6 have no 2000 value.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-f (interpolation between the anchors);
D-2026-10-05-k (consequence for the nine); D-2026-10-10-g.
**Assertion.** `03-controls-gdp.R`, raw-state block (column names, 5,566
rows, 2022 header cells, 5,570 municipalities in 2022, anchors positive).

## Q3. Do Santarém and Mojuí dos Campos recover the combined pre-2013 total?

```{r q3-pair}
pair <- gdp %>%
  filter(geocode %in% c("1506807", "1504752"), year %in% c(2002, 2010:2014, 2022)) %>%
  select(geocode, year, population, gdp_brl)
pair %>% pivot_wider(names_from = geocode, values_from = c(population, gdp_brl))
santarem_raw <- pib_raw %>%
  filter(geocode == "1506807", year %in% c(2002, 2010:2014, 2022)) %>%
  transmute(year, santarem_served = as.numeric(value) * 1000)
pair %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(pair_gdp = sum(gdp_brl), .groups = "drop") %>%
  inner_join(santarem_raw, by = "year") %>%
  mutate(diff = pair_gdp - santarem_served)
```

**Finding.** Before 2013 the two series sum exactly to Santarém's served
GDP (and the same holds for population, asserted in the script); from 2013
each municipality has its own series, so the pair's total exceeds
Santarém's. Mojuí receives about 5.6 percent of the pair's GDP and 6.6
percent of its population, the 2022 shares.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-10-e.
**Assertion.** `03-controls-gdp.R`, output block (pair sums equal the
served values before 2013).

## Q4. Which municipalities lack GDP per capita before 2010, and what do the official estimates say?

What is checked: the sample municipalities with NA population in the GDP
years, and the Tabela 6579 estimates for the same municipality-years.

```{r q4-missing}
gdp %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode, is.na(population)) %>%
  left_join(sample_geo, by = "geocode") %>%
  group_by(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation) %>%
  summarise(years = paste(range(year), collapse = "-"), n = n(),
            gdp_present = sum(!is.na(gdp_brl)), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r q4-estimates}
list.files(sidra_dir, pattern = "^sidra_6579_")
est <- est_raw %>% transmute(geocode, year, estimate = sidra_value(value, character(0)))
gdp %>%
  filter(geocode == "5103254", year <= 2012) %>%
  select(year, population, gdp_brl) %>%
  left_join(est %>% filter(geocode == "5103254") %>% select(year, estimate), by = "year")
```

**Finding.** The nine Mato Grosso municipalities installed after 2000 have
GDP from 2002 (seven of them) or 2005 (Ipiranga do Norte, Itanhangá) but no
population before 2010, so their GDP per capita is NA for 2002-2009; this
is why Colniza drops from every covariate-adjusted specification
(D-2026-10-05-k). Tabela 6579 carries official estimates for 2001-2006,
2008-2009, 2011-2021 and 2024 onward (2007 was a population count, 2010
and 2022 censuses, 2023 is not served) for every one of them from their
installation, the input task 1.6 will splice in.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-k (closed, consequence); task 1.6 open; the
estimates are not used in phase 1.
**Assertion.** `03-controls-gdp.R`, output block (population missing only
before a municipality's first census, Mojuí excepted).

## Q5. How far is the interpolated population from the official estimates?

```{r q5-deviation}
gdp %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode, !is.na(population)) %>%
  inner_join(est, by = c("geocode", "year")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(estimate)) %>%
  mutate(rel = population / estimate - 1) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), median_rel = median(rel), p10 = quantile(rel, 0.10),
            p90 = quantile(rel, 0.90), .groups = "drop")
```

**Finding.** Through 2009 the median deviation stays within one percent,
with the 10-90 range widening to about -17/+26 percent in the middle of
the decade, where a straight line between censuses departs most from the
estimated path. From 2011 the median drifts to -6.7 percent by 2021: the
line toward the 2022 census, which came in below the projected estimates,
runs under them, and the range reaches -26/+11 percent. The deviation is
the cost of D-2026-10-05-f, to be weighed in tasks 1.6 and 1.7.
**Decision.** none in phase 1 (tasks 1.6, 1.7).

## Q6. For which years is population stored?

```{r q6-years}
gdp %>% filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), population_na = sum(is.na(population)), gdp_na = sum(is.na(gdp_brl)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(year <= 2004 | year >= 2020)
```

**Finding.** The output starts in 2002 with the GDP series and ends in
2022 with the last census, so the panel has no population for 2000 and
2001 although the 2000 census anchor exists. The 2023 GDP release is read
and dropped by the year cap.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-10-k (open).
**Assertion.** `03-controls-gdp.R`, output block (row count 5,570 x 21
years).
